hypothesis.statement: A single persistent auxiliary stream may retain most of the Stage08 scheduling benefit while halving auxiliary stream/Lt state ownership and reducing each attention boundary from three records plus four waits to two records plus two waits.
hypothesis.fixed_axes: Exact B29/CC10.3/19x19/FP16/NHWC, the complete id70/tile23/stages35/cluster5 tuple, alpha=1, beta=0, Q/K/V buffers, RoPE, FA4, and every other retained tactic remain unchanged.

temporary_implementation.ownership_per_outer_handle: one persistent nonblocking aux stream, one independent cuBLASLt handle/plan/private workspace, one ready event, and one done event
dag_per_attention: K id70 then V id70 launch sequentially on the one aux stream and one Lt state
aux records one done event after V
primary waits done before retained RoPE/FA4

same_binary_symmetric_short.method: exact B29/S2, 50 warmups and 300 timed forwards, control-aux1-aux2-aux2-aux1-control

root_difficulty.static_dag: The single aux stream imposes a FIFO K->V edge. At the fork, only Q and K are dependency-ready; V cannot become ready until K completes. Aux1 therefore recreates a two-grid frontier, whereas retained aux2 exposes Q, K, and V as three sibling grids per outer lane and six across S2.
root_difficulty.measured_conclusion: Reducing four event operations per attention is much smaller than the loss from serializing K/V readiness. Aux1 barely beats the no-aux control and loses a clear 2.000% to aux2.
root_difficulty.why_no_profiler_or_replay: The predeclared gate closes aux1 when it does not beat aux2 in the same-binary symmetric short test. NSYS, replay, request gate, and long testing cannot change the failed topology ranking and were intentionally not run.

decision.reason: One aux stream saves event APIs but fails to expose V as a sibling ready grid; the retained two-aux topology is 2.000% faster in the fixed symmetric comparison.
